Omit it otherwise.opportunitiesTen to twenty words for the notifier's own ledger. Never shown to the user.The candidate's number in the packet's Candidates section.The turn's number in the packet's Conversation since the last edition section.The opening line the user reads before the items, in a peer voice, plain text. Empty only when the edition has no items.Stable source/object reference plus the specific useful outcome or material state change. Reuse the key in shared history for the same matter; do not change it for paraphrasing, a new day, another source, or richer formatting.The candidate numbers this item settles. Every item requires a candidate; follow_up requires a prepared opportunity.The numbers of the conversation turns this item rests on or follows up on, as the packet numbers them. At least one for follow_up; otherwise only when a turn grounds the item, so omit or leave empty when none does.offer = Muse can act and the message ends with the offer; carries an action. heads_up = a time-bound fact with a consequence; asks nothing. letter = one line announcing a ready Letter. follow_up = one gentle check-in on something the user left open in the conversation; at most one per edition.A short title naming what the item concerns. Plain text.The line the user reads, in a peer voice, plain text. An offer ends with the offer question.brief = the message is the whole item. deep = the user must read more than a line; details carry the rest.Markdown for a deep item only: what the user reads past the message. Null on brief items.The action in a few words, as a button would read.The request Muse runs when the user says yes, written as the user would ask it.Required on an offer: the action Muse takes on a yes. Null otherwise.Select zero, one, or several independently worthwhile items. The item bound is a payload safety limit, never a target. Leave empty when nothing earns attention.Your recommendation for the form. widget when the edition has a shape worth seeing or a choice worth a tap (an offer or a heads-up that turns on one date, number, place, or comparison); text when it is a line of conversation; artifact when prepared work deserves a page, including several related items. The delivering turn decides the final form.Candidates left out only because their moment is later than the next edition, each by its number. They stay pending.Every other candidate you left out, each by its number. messages.description: At most one focused message at each priority. Empty means no delivery. Selected work carries its original preparation, action and sources.

items.description: Copy the supplied item:N labels of work serving this one situation.

handoff.description: Explain what matters, what is ready, remaining uncertainty and decisions, and any checks needed at delivery. Include sources and dates for new findings.

priority.description: Omit for regular. High needs a concrete consequence of waiting beyond today.

overrides.description: Usually omit. By selected item:N label, specify only a changed kind or action, or additional evidence. Explain the change in the handoff.

kind.description: Omit to infer from the original Letter or final action. Use follow_up for grounded follow-through on something the user left open.

action.description: The exact action to propose after the remaining choice or permission is resolved. Omit to inherit the prepared action.

evidence.description: Additional source:N labels or original URLs, file paths or record identifiers you read. Original evidence is already included. Explain what these support in the handoff.

drop.description: Optional item:N labels to discard because the work is unsupported, unwanted or already handled.

revisit.description: Optional item:N labels mapped to useful future reconsideration times. Omitted work stays pending until expiry; null keeps the ordinary schedule.
